newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Brown blames rate rise on government.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Brown blames rate rise on government.

text.p: Wednesday's rise in UK interest rates was not due to international pressures or the strength of the domestic economy, Gordon Brown, economics spokesman of the main opposition Labour party, said.
He told Parliament the rise was inevitable because of the government's failure to tackle the underlying weakness of the economy, leaving it vulnerable to a resurgence of inflation.

Brown, accusing Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke of complacency in describing Britain's investment record, said interest rates were higher now than in ten other European countries, while inflation was above the European average.
The government's longer-term growth record since it took power in 1979 also put Britain at the bottom of the Group of Seven league table, he said during a debate on the economy.

"You would think after today that the Chancellor's claims about the economy would be more modest," Brown said, accusing the government of deceit in painting an over-rosy picture of Britain's economic prospects.

Britain had fallen from 13th to 18th place in the world economic league and had slipped into the second half of the European league table. It was only the ninth richest out of the 15 European Union members, Brown said.
